> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `07d48d46b8b905e1e3f39df660bbfcda8f5fd336` — the merge of head `d9fe9175e7d7e9e702ffc21fe0dd6b7fd13bfdeb` into base `4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 07d48d46b8b905e1e3f39df660bbfcda8f5fd336 && git checkout 07d48d46b8b905e1e3f39df660bbfcda8f5fd336
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3 d9fe9175e7d7e9e702ffc21fe0dd6b7fd13bfdeb && git checkout -B drift-repro 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3 && git merge --no-ff d9fe9175e7d7e9e702ffc21fe0dd6b7fd13bfdeb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### L1 review (#35142) · 2026-11-18T09:27Z

L1: REWORK (one must-fix in the changeset; the code is accepted)
Head-sha: 03e8ce4f42cf115474d0b7582a4bfee58b074cb8

This is the first L1 on this PR. I read the full diff against the merge base `99a0e4fbfc`: 3 files, +200 / −5. I also read the card, claim 6972293717, re-claim 6972714855, trace 6972487188 and os-dev report 6974362299, and I compared the `update` door against `@objectstack/objectql@18.5.0`.

**The fix (route A).**
- `UpdateFacet.update` no longer re-enters itself inside `inAfterAbortUnit` at the door. It computes `ownUnit` once from the same `opensAfterAbortUnit('afterUpdate', …)` predicate, which is unchanged. It then wraps only the executor it hands to `executeWithMiddleware`, so the middleware chain, including the authorization gate's reads, runs before BEGIN.
- The `before*` dispatch, the row write, the `after*` chain and the secret-handle release stay inside the executor, so they are inside the unit and still roll back together. That is what `HookSchema.onError` `abort` and #34412 need.
- I checked what else moved out of the unit, which is the door code between `resolveObjectName` and the executor:
  - `assertWriteAllowed`, the organization-probe invalidation and the option folding are pure.
  - `enforceTransactionOrigin` gives the same answer: the unit only opens on the default driver, so inside it the scope was same-origin anyway.
  - `withResolvedWhere` is a read.
  - There is no write between the door and the executor.
  - Inside the executor, the unit reaches the writes through the ambient store, as it did before.

**The two questions you asked.**
1. *Middleware code after `next()` now runs after the commit.* Accepted. It makes a hooked update behave like every update that opens no unit, which is how a middleware's post-`next()` work has always run in the common case. The `sys_member` org-admin reconcile writes (`security-plugin-start-hooks.ts:533` / `:556`) were in the row's unit only when a *metadata* hook binds `sys_member`, because code-registered hooks open no unit (the #22782 line). On every deployment without such a hook they already ran after the commit. Nothing in `docs/adr`, `content/docs` or `skills` names the door-level unit: `opensAfterAbortUnit` and `#22782` have 0 hits there.
2. *Contract face.* None by surface. There is no `packages/spec` path, no published export, signature, error code or schema change, and no governed path. The loser's answer moves back to the `409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE` that ADR-0142 D4 states. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right, and no L2 is owed.

**Shape and scope.**
- `Fixes #35142` is on the first card line, with no closing keyword next to another open card.
- The paths are inside the re-claim: `objectql/src/**`, new test files and one changeset.
- `check-governed-merges --pr 35165`: not governed, +200 / −5.
- The changeset bumps `@objectstack/objectql` at `patch` and is new, not on `main`.

**Tests and evidence.**
- `ownership-claim-race-sqlite.test.ts` runs 4 cells × 25 rounds, crossing a private or public OWD with a hooked or unhooked object, through the real plugin-security middleware on SQLite. Each round asserts exactly one landed claim and every loser at `409`. On `main` the hooked cells were 404×25 and 403×25. Here it was green over 4 runs of 100 rounds per cell.
- Two cases keep the gate's own refusals: a row that is gone answers `404`, and a row the caller cannot read answers not-found, never forbidden.
- The ablation turned the pin red, and the restore was verified.
- objectql: 13,791 tests passed. Gates: 68 of 70 exit 0, and 2 are declared NOT MEASURED (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n`, which need dists). Both run in CI, which is green.

**CI at this head**, from check-runs: 37 success, 16 skipped, none failed or in progress.

#### Must-fix
- **M1. The changeset names only half the scope the change has.** `ownUnit` is `opensAfterAbortUnit`'s whole answer. That is true for a metadata `beforeUpdate` hook (`sideWriting`, #34412, new in 18.6.0), and also for a blocking `abort` or conditioned metadata `afterUpdate` hook (`aborting`, #22782). The door-level unit for the second kind already shipped in 18.5.0 (`engine-update.ts:151-153` at `@objectstack/objectql@18.5.0`). So for an object with only such an `afterUpdate` hook:
  - the loser's `404` / `403` was not "since 18.6.0": it predates it, and this PR fixes it too;
  - "What a middleware does after `next()` … now runs after the commit" is a change from every earlier release, not a return to the pre-18.6.0 behaviour that the report's reading suggests.
  
  The title ("on an object with a metadata `beforeUpdate` hook") and the cause paragraph both say only the `beforeUpdate` half. Fix: say that the change applies to any update that opens its own unit, meaning a metadata `beforeUpdate` hook or a blocking or conditioned metadata `afterUpdate` hook. Give the race answer's history for each, and keep the post-`next()` sentence for both. This is a changeset (and PR body) change only. I'll read that delta, plus CI at the new head.

#### Should-fix
- **S1. Pin the `afterUpdate` arm too.** The four cells bind only a `beforeUpdate` hook. One more hooked cell, with an object whose only metadata hook is a blocking `afterUpdate`, would hold the second arm of the same predicate to `409`. A private OWD at the same 25 rounds is enough. If you decline, say why in the delta request.

#### Notes
- **N1. Verb asymmetry.** `insert` and `delete` keep the door-level unit, so their middleware's post-`next()` work stays inside the unit while `update`'s now does not. The report measured `insert` as symmetric for the race, and recorded the delete loser's `false` vs `404`. A follow-up card that decides whether the other two verbs should move the same way would close this. It does not block this PR.
- **Owed after L1, not mine.** Nothing at L2. Landing: hotcrm#2634 waits on this.

### L1 review, delta for REWORK 6974452034 (#35142) · 2026-11-18T11:17Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: d9fe9175e7d7e9e702ffc21fe0dd6b7fd13bfdeb
Delta read: 03e8ce4f42 → d9fe9175e7. The three commits 415eefd791 (pin), 99c200dbb1 and d9fe9175e7 (changeset) touch 2 files, +60 / −38. `engine-update.ts` is not touched, so the code I accepted in 6974452034 is unchanged.

**M1, closed.**
- The changeset title now covers "any update that opens its own unit of work".
- The body names both arms of `opensAfterAbortUnit`, each with its own history:
  - a metadata `beforeUpdate` hook opens the unit from 18.6.0, so the race answer was 409 in 18.5.0, 404/403 in 18.6.0, and is 409 again here;
  - a blocking or conditioned metadata `afterUpdate` hook already opened it in 18.5.0, so the answer was 404/403 in both releases and is 409 here for the first time.
- The post-`next()` sentence now covers both arms. For the `afterUpdate` arm it says plainly that this is a change, not a return: the code ran inside the unit from 18.0.0 through 18.6.0.
- I re-checked that history at the tags. At `@objectstack/objectql@18.0.0`, `engine.ts` has the door re-entry `inAfterAbortUnit(() => this.update…)` (1 hit). `@objectstack/objectql@17.7.0` has no `inAfterAbortUnit` at all (0 hits). At 18.5.0 the re-entry is at `engine-update.ts:151-153`.
- The PR body says the same in both languages, and it carries the `sys_member` reconcile line for each arm.

**S1, taken.**
- The fifth cell is `private` OWD on an object whose only metadata hook is a blocking `afterUpdate` (`onError: 'abort'`), run for 25 rounds. It asserts the same things as the other four cells: one claim lands, every loser gets `CONCURRENT_UPDATE/409`, and the stored owner is the winner.
- Report 6976908794 records the cell red on `main`'s `engine-update.ts`, at `RECORD_NOT_FOUND/404` in all 25 rounds, and green on the fix.
- The four existing cells and the two non-regression cases are unchanged apart from the `hook` parameter.

**N1** is carried by #35167 (whether insert and delete should get the same change).

**Gates.** 70 of 70 exit 0, with `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` measured this time.

**CI at this head**, from check-runs: 39 success, 18 skipped, none failed or in progress.

#### Must-fix
None.

#### Should-fix
None.

#### Notes
- **Owed after L1, not mine.** Nothing at L2, as before (no contract face). Landing: hotcrm#2634 is waiting on this.
